issues.label: Jurisdiction properly assumed over JS
issues.why: The court must confirm statutory jurisdiction under the child protective proceeding framework was validly established at adjudication.

issues.label: Ground (b)(i): sexual abuse by parent
issues.why: Court must determine whether clear and convincing evidence shows respondent caused sexual abuse and likelihood of future harm.

issues.label: Ground (k)(ii): criminal sexual conduct/penetration
issues.why: Court must assess whether the conduct meets the specific statutory definition, including whether penetration or the required act occurred.

issues.label: Whether penetration occurred
issues.why: Respondent denied vaginal penetration, which may be dispositional for the (k)(ii) ground's definitional requirements.

issues.label: Sexual purpose vs. legitimate hygiene
issues.why: Respondent claimed bathing was for cleaning after accidents, requiring the court to resolve intent.

issues.label: Reliability of child's SANE disclosures
issues.why: JS's out-of-court statements and demonstrations are central and their credibility and admissibility must be weighed.

issues.label: Admissibility of child hearsay statements
issues.why: JS did not testify, so the statements' admissibility under applicable hearsay/tender-years rules must be evaluated.

issues.label: Weight of UTI/medical evidence
issues.why: The positive UTI and irritation must be assessed as corroboration versus alternative innocent causes.

issues.label: Relevance of attraction to half-sister
issues.why: Respondent's statements about the half-sister bear on propensity/intent and their probative value must be weighed.

issues.label: Clear and convincing evidence standard applied
issues.why: Court must ensure the heightened statutory burden was met for each termination ground.

issues.label: Best-interests determination by preponderance
issues.why: Court must find termination serves JS's best interests under the correct lower standard.

issues.label: Parent-child bond in best interests
issues.why: Siblings' testimony of a strong bond must be weighed against risk in the best-interests analysis.

issues.label: Non-custodial parent status considerations
issues.why: Respondent's non-custodial role and near-daily visitation affect risk and best-interests calculus.

issues.label: Termination at initial disposition permissibility
issues.why: Court must confirm statutory authority to terminate at initial disposition without offering reunification services.

issues.label: Reasonable efforts / aggravated circumstances
issues.why: Whether reunification efforts were required or excused due to sexual abuse aggravating circumstances.

issues.label: Placement with relative consideration
issues.why: JS remained with her mother, and relative placement can weigh against termination in best interests.

issues.label: Credibility determinations among witnesses
issues.why: Court must resolve conflicting testimony from respondent, siblings, mother, and investigators.

issues.label: Behavioral-change evidence probative value
issues.why: Night terrors, itching, and fear must be assessed as circumstantial indicators of abuse.

issues.label: Sending JS home without underwear
issues.why: This conduct must be weighed as circumstantial evidence of grooming or abuse.

issues.label: Whether same evidence supports both grounds and best interests
issues.why: Court must independently analyze statutory grounds and best interests without conflating them.
